newsitem.title: CANADA: Gandalf shares dive on news of cash woes.
newsitem.headline: Gandalf shares dive on news of cash woes.

text.p: Shares in Gandalf Technologies Inc dropped on Friday after the troubled computer company said it was almost out of money and was mulling several offers for its business that are substantially below its market value.

The Nepean, Ontario-based computer network equipment maker said in a statement release after market close yesterday that it has exceeded its available margin amount on its Royal Bank of Canada credit line. The line was cut to C$13 million from C$20 million when Gandalf reported poor fiscal 1997 fourth quarter results last month and fell into technical default on its loan.

The stock tumbled 1.10 to 1.50 on the Toronto Stock Exchange shortly after the open before recovering slightly to trade down 0.80 at 1.80 in turnover of more than 770,000 shares. It was down 20/32 to 1-5/16 on Nasdaq.
Analysts likened Thursday's statement to an obituary.
"Why wouldn't the stock crash (after that release)? I'm surprised it's as high as it is," one analyst said.
Another New York-based analyst said the writing has been on the wall since the stock fell on Nasdaq from more than US$18 in May 1996 to about US$5 in eight weeks.
"I personally said sayonara to the thing at $14," he said.
